text:
A bank hack would be far worse than a crypto exchange hack.

ARK Invest's Brett Winton says a bank hack could freeze the financial system, showing why holding Bitcoin could pay off

"If a major crypto exchange got hacked in a profound way, literally the assets could be transferred onchain to somebody else, and then somebody else owns them. Big problem."

"On the other hand, it's kind of a simple problem. Somebody else has the private keys. These are effectively bearer instruments."

"If somebody goes into a bank, they wouldn't necessarily be able to take the money. But they could totally scramble the accounts of the bank in a way where it would actually be a much bigger problem for the financial system if we didn't know where the money was."

"Who owes money to who suddenly gets called into question, and it would totally freeze the local financial ecosystem, and depending on the size of the bank could severely arrest the global financial ecosystem."

"In those circumstances, if you have Bitcoin or any crypto asset that is digitally secured, you'd be like, well, at least I know I have this. I do think it's illustrative of the potential option value of the asset."

zh_summary: $ASTS 可能在 2027 年預訂 13 次火箭發射、2031 年達 32 次，僅八次 Falcon 9 與兩次 New Glenn 即可在 2027 年搭載約 40 顆 BlueBird 衛星，接近關鍵市場持續覆蓋所需的約 45 顆。儘管透過 Starlink Mobile 直接競爭，$SPCX 到 2031 年仍可能佔其發射的一半。替代發射商至關重要，Piper 預計 $RKLB Neutron 從 2028 年一次 AST 發射增至 2030 年每年四次。
en_summary: $ASTS could book 13 rocket launches in 2027 and 32 by 2031, with eight Falcon 9 and two New Glenn potentially carrying ~40 BlueBird satellites in 2027, nearing the ~45 needed for continuous coverage in key markets. $SPCX could still account for half its launches by 2031 despite competing via Starlink Mobile. Alternative providers matter, with Piper projecting $RKLB Neutron from one AST launch in 2028 to four annually by 2030.
ko_summary: $ASTS는 2027년에 13회, 2031년까지 32회의 로켓 발사를 예약할 수 있으며, 단 8회의 Falcon 9와 2회의 New Glenn으로 2027년에 약 40개의 BlueBird 위성을 탑재해 주요 시장 지속 커버리지에 필요한 약 45개에 가까워질 수 있다. Starlink Mobile을 통한 직접 경쟁에도 불구하고 $SPCX는 2031년까지 발사의 절반을 차지할 수 있다. 대체 발사 업체가 중요하며, Piper는 $RKLB Neutron이 2028년 AST 발사 1회에서 2030년 연간 4회로 늘어날 것으로 전망한다.
text:
$ASTS could book 13 rocket launches in 2027 and 32 by 2031 with just eight Falcon 9 and two New Glenn flights potentially carrying ~40 BlueBird satellites in 2027.

That could bring ASTS much closer to the ~45 satellites needed for continuous coverage in key markets but whats really interesting is that $SPCX could still account for half its launches by 2031 despite competing directly through Starlink Mobile.

That makes having alternative launch providers huge with Piper projecting $RKLB Neutron could go from one AST launch in 2028 to four annually by 2030 as Rocket Lab becomes another potential option for expanding the constellation.

ticker_notes.BE: turbines lose cost edge, long lead times

zh_summary: @StockSavvyShay：$BE 故事中被忽視的部分是燃氣渦輪機正在失去成本優勢，到 2030 年成本預計上升約 3.5 倍至每千瓦 3000 美元，而 Bloom 燃料電池約 3900 美元/千瓦。渦輪機交貨期長達 7 年，Bloom 可直接在資料中心發電而無需等待電網。$NVDA CEO Jensen Huang 估計 1GW AI 工廠每年可產生約 400 億美元，因此三個月延遲可能損失約 100 億美元營收，使更快獲得電力的價值遠超前期節省。
en_summary: @StockSavvyShay: Overlooked part of $BE story is gas turbines losing cost advantage, costs rising ~3.5x to $3,000/kW by 2030 while Bloom fuel cell ~$3,900/kW. Turbine lead times up to 7 years, Bloom can power data centers without grid wait. $NVDA Jensen Huang estimates 1GW AI factory ~$40B annually, so 3-month delay ~$10B lost revenue, making faster power worth more than upfront savings.
ko_summary: @StockSavvyShay: $BE 스토리에서 간과된 부분은 가스 터빈이 비용 우위를 잃고 있으며, 2030년까지 비용이 약 3.5배 상승해 kW당 3000달러에 이르는 반면 Bloom 연료전지는 약 3900달러/kW이다. 터빈 리드타임은 7년까지 늘어나고, Bloom은 그리드 연결을 기다리지 않고 데이터센터에서 직접 전력을 생산할 수 있다. $NVDA CEO Jensen Huang은 1GW AI 공장이 연간 약 400억 달러를 창출할 것으로 추정하므로 3개월 지연은 약 100억 달러 매출 손실을 의미하며, 더 빠른 전력 확보가 초기 비용 절감보다 가치가 크다.
text:
I think one of most overlooked parts of the $BE story is how quickly gas turbines are losing their cost advantage with costs projected to rise ~3.5x to $3,000/kW by 2030 while Bloom's fuel cell pricing reaches ~$3,900/kW.

That gap becomes even more interesting when turbine lead times are stretching as long as 7 years and Bloom can generate power directly at data centers without waiting on traditional grid connections.

And when $NVDA CEO Jensen Huang estimates a 1 GW AI factory could generate ~$40B annually then even a three-month delay could mean ~$10B in lost revenue which is why getting power online faster could be worth far more than saving on upfront equipment costs.

text:

This chart puts things into perspective with Neutron's estimated ~26-month delay below the ~40-month industry average and I'd much rather see Rocket Lab fix its manufacturing issues than rush its first launch.

And Iridium's recurring satellite revenue and Rocket Lab's growing space systems business give them multiple growth engines as it builds a credible reusable launch alternative to SpaceX.

ticker_notes.AMD: Trades at ~47x forward earnings with exp

zh_summary: 這是Peter Lynch最喜歡的指標，將估值與增長掛鉤，偏好使用2026至2028年窗口，以便倍數根據業務實際複合成長速度調整。例如$AMD以約47倍遠期盈利交易，但盈利預計從2026年的5.71美元增長至2028年的20.29美元，意味著約89%的盈利CAGR和約0.5倍的PEG。
en_summary: This is Peter Lynch’s favorite metric tying valuation to growth, preferring a 2026 to 2028 window so the multiple adjusts for how fast the business is compounding. For example $AMD trades at ~47x forward earnings but earnings expected to grow from $5.71 in 2026 to $20.29 in 2028 implying ~89% earnings CAGR and PEG of ~0.5x.
ko_summary: 이것은 Peter Lynch의 가장 좋아하는 지표로 밸류에이션을 성장에 연결하며, 2026년부터 2028년 창을 선호하여 배수가 사업이 실제로 복리 성장하는 속도에 맞게 조정되도록 한다. 예를 들어 $AMD는 약 47배 포워드 수익에 거래되지만 수익이 2026년 $5.71에서 2028년 $20.29로 성장할 것으로 예상되어 약 89%의 수익 CAGR과 약 0.5x의 PEG를 의미한다.
text:
This is Peter Lynch’s favorite metric and I like it too because it ties valuation to growth and I prefer using a 2026 to 2028 window so the multiple adjusts for how fast the business is actually compounding.

For example $AMD trades at ~47x forward earnings but earnings are expected to grow from $5.71 in 2026 to $20.29 in 2028 implying a ~89% earnings CAGR and PEG of ~0.5x.

zh_summary: @SJosephBurns解釋損失10%交易資本仍有90%在運作，只需11%回報即可回本。損失50%則需將剩餘資本翻倍。損失80%只剩每元20分。回撤不僅拿走金錢，還拿走恢復損失所需的資本。避免大回撤以留在遊戲中。
en_summary: @SJosephBurns explains that losing 10% of trading capital leaves 90% working, needing 11% to recover. Losing 50% requires doubling remaining capital. Losing 80% leaves 20 cents on the dollar. Drawdowns take away capital needed to recover losses. Avoid big drawdowns to stay in the game.
ko_summary: @SJosephBurns는 거래 자본의 10%를 잃어도 90%가 작동하며 11% 수익률로 회복할 수 있다고 설명합니다. 50%를 잃으면 남은 자본을 두 배로 늘려야 합니다. 80%를 잃으면 원래 달러당 20센트만 남습니다. 드로다운은 손실을 회복하는 데 필요한 자본을 빼앗습니다. 큰 드로다운을 피해 게임에 머물러세요.
text:
Lose 10% of your trading capital and you still have 90% of your capital working for you to get back to your equity peak. You just need an 11% return to get back to even. 

Lose 50% and half your capital has disappeared while your required recovery to get back to even requires doubling your remaining capital. 

Lose 80% and you're trying to rebuild with only 20 cents of every original dollar. You’re destroyed. 

Drawdowns don't just take your money. They take away the capital needed to make back your losses. 

Avoid big drawdowns above all else to stay in the game.

text:
Few things:

- $SIVE is targeting T1 hyperscaler deployments for pluggables, CPO, NPO. Not quite sure what you mean by Tier 2. 

They have direct engagements with hyperscalers but currently are more upstream by qualifying with companies like Ayar, $JBL, $GFS, O-Net that eventually likely ends up -> $AMZN / $MSFT for example. 

On financing: 

- Colo players like $CIFR still need $1B+ of financing for their sites.
- Neoclouds like $CRWV need billions of financing to buy GPUs.

Higher rates + less support for financing makes it more challenging for these players. 

$SIVE already raised 700M SEK for their buildout and largely rely on external foundries, so they don't have financing constraints. 

There's pressure on players that need currently need financing for capex, but markets group up everyone in AI sector indiscriminately. 

The second nuance is whether or not this effects the end customers in terms of demand. 

I'd argue optical sector is insulated, even if overall AI capex from hyperscalers decreases, I see optical content still rising and aggregate demand rising. 

And this is especially the case with new incoming players going through their first qual cycles.

text:
The people actually building the AI infrastructure are describing incredible demand and a multi-year supply shortage. The market is worrying about a bubble.  

$AMZN CEO Andy Jassy: Even with $220B in 2026 capex, Amazon is still leaving meaningful demand on the table. 2026 sold out. 2027 largely sold out. Good chunk of 2028 already booked.  

$SPCX CEO Elon Musk: Demand is overwhelming supply. New compute is paying back in under a year. Shortage will last a long time. Power and construction are the real bottlenecks.  

$NVDA CEO Jensen Huang: Neocloud demand is “off the charts.” Orders keep coming. Bottlenecks keep shifting (chips → packaging → HBM → power) and will last for years. The missing piece is capital, not demand.  

Stocks are down because of financing stress, higher rates and FCF optics - not because utilisation, backlog or rental pricing collapsed.   

When operators with the best visibility are still constrained and sold out well into 2027–28, the recent selloff looks more like a positioning reset than a demand air-pocket.  

This is usually when the better opportunities show up. Remember the adage "Buy fear, sell euphoria."

text:
AI agents are already accessing bank accounts and trying to move money, per Axios.

Banks are scrambling to restrict them. Could be a pretty interesting setup for some of the smaller cyber names.

$OSPN already serves more than 60% of the world's 100 largest banks, according to its investor deck.

They already sell those banks authentication and transaction security. Now add agents logging in, buying things and making payments for customers.

The bank has to know who gave the agent access, what it's allowed to do, and which transactions still need the customer's approval.

I think banks could end up spending a lot more on this as agent use grows. $OSPN already has relationships with many of the banks that would be buying.

$MITK, $YOU and a few others are also names I like here.

Disclosure: I'm long $OSPN.

name: Kris Sidial🇺🇸
zh_summary: 大型市場波動往往需要雙向行動，因為另一方參與者最終會平倉，儲存能量加速波動。含義不明確的灰色催化劑通過吸引對立觀點來維持這種動態，直到資本約束迫使交易。例子包括2020年3月COVID期間抄底者和波動率賣方助長進一步下跌，以及2021年1月迷因狂熱中GameStop和AMC的空頭為上漲增添燃料。
en_summary: Large market moves often need two-way action because participants on the other side eventually unwind, storing energy that accelerates the move. Gray catalysts with unclear implications sustain this by attracting opposing views until capital constraints force transactions. Examples include COVID in March 2020 where dip buyers and vol sellers fueled further declines, and meme mania in January 2021 with GameStop and AMC where shorts added fuel to the surge.
ko_summary: 대형 시장 움직임은 종종 양방향 행동이 필요하다. 반대편 참가자들이 결국 포지션을 청산하면서 에너지를 저장해 움직임을 가속화하기 때문이다. 함의가 불명확한 회색 촉매는 자본 제약으로 거래가 강제될 때까지 반대 견해를 끌어들여 이를 지속시킨다. 예로는 2020년 3월 COVID 때 하락 매수자와 변동성 매도자가 추가 하락을 부추긴 경우와 2021년 1월 밈 열풍에서 GameStop과 AMC의 공매도가 급등에 연료를 더한 경우가 있다.
text:
By nature of being a vol trader, I’ve studied many different market crashes. Not just the common ones in the U.S., but episodes like Britain in 1720, Vienna in 1873, and the Dutch tulip mania of 1637.

There are some interesting behavioral takeaways that aren’t entirely intuitive unless you participate in markets every single day.

One of the biggest for me is that large market moves often need two-way action to develop. Behaviorally, you need participants willing to take the other side, because their eventual need to unwind can help accelerate the move. It’s almost like storing energy that gets released later. To create that dynamic, a “gray catalyst” can be particularly powerful one whose implications aren’t immediately black and white. 

Here are two examples that helped produce massive moves in opposite directions that had gray area headlines that led to that two way flow. 

COVID (March 2020): What often gets lost in the sauce is that many participants were aggressively betting against the idea that COVID would be severely disruptive. As stocks fell, they bought the dip and sold vol. When stocks kept falling and vol kept rising, some of those positions became fuel for the next leg of the move as participants were forced to unwind.

Looking back, the outcome seems obvious. In real time, the eventual scale of the disruption was far from clear. There was HOPE that it would pass quickly. Headlines about potential treatments, policy support, or a less severe impact repeatedly

The proportion of S&P 500 stocks trading above their 50-day moving average surged +5 percentage points on Friday, to 61%, the highest reading since mid-August.

Since the October 1st intraday low, this figure has more than tripled.

Additionally, the proportion of S&P 500 stocks trading above their 200-day moving average rose +3 percentage points on Friday, to 57%, the most since September 9th.

Over the last 3 weeks, this figure has risen +17 percentage points.

This comes despite the S&P 500 remaining roughly unchanged over the same period.

This also ranks among the 3 sharpest improvements in market breadth over the last 3 years.

On Thursday alone, 335 S&P 500 stocks finished higher, despite the index declining -1.2% on that day.

The market is strengthening beneath the surface.

ko_summary: @Ksidiii: 공매도 잔고 차트를 공유하는 이들은 자금 흐름을 놓친다. 대부분은 순수 숏 베팅이 아니라, 투기적 베팅에 대차대조표를 제공하는 은행이 증거금 완화를 위해 고객에게 더 많은 숏 노출을 요구하는 것.
text:
Everyone who keeps sharing these short interest charts is missing the flows behind them. Most shops are not taking outright short bets. This is another effort to ease margin requirements across the street: banks providing balance sheet for more speculative bets are asking clients to post more short exposure.

The sequence on the street looks like this:

HF manager: “I want more margin.”

Bank: “Things look risky in public AI bets, and we’re already lending a lot against private AI bets. For some clients, we’ll extend more financing, but only if they add more short exposure to improve their collateral scores.”

HF manager: “Okay, I’ll short more stock against my main bet.”

That is how you end up with short exposures that look astronomically high while many end users remain heavily long tech. The additional shorts are supporting the financing of their main bets.

Which also tells the bigger story on why raw equity financing rates haven’t blown out the way they did ahead of the big SpaceX IPO in June, despite the fact that lending is slowing.

ko_summary: (@elonmusk에 의해 리포스트됨) @EvaFox는 2002년 초 Elon이 SpaceX를 출범시키려던 중 80파운드 로켓 엔진을 들고 있는 Tom Mueller를 발견했다고 말합니다. 이는 아마추어가 만든 최대 액체 연료 엔진으로 13,000파운드 추력을 가졌습니다. Elon은 더 큰 것을 만들 수 있는지 물었고, 그들은 첫 SpaceX 로켓을 스케치했으며, Tom은 1호 직원이 되어 Merlin, Kestrel, Draco 엔진을 만들었습니다.
text:
In early 2002, Elon was preparing to launch SpaceX and searching for the people who could help him build a rocket from scratch. One Sunday in January 2002, he walked into a friend's rented warehouse in Huntington Beach and found Tom Mueller holding an 80-pound rocket engine on his shoulder, trying to bolt it to a frame. It was the largest liquid-fuel engine any amateur had ever built, with 13,000 pounds of thrust, made in Tom's spare time. 

Elon asked the main question  “Could you build something bigger?”

The next Sunday Elon came to his house. It was Super Bowl Sunday; they watched maybe one play, because they were too busy sketching the first SpaceX rocket.

Tom became SpaceX employee #1, and the man who built engines on weekends went on to build Merlin, Kestrel and Draco. 

Elon saw a person, not a résumé, someone who built rockets with his own hands simply because he loved them.
